title: feat(qa): skill-evals grader takes an any-of form; objectstack-ai case 6 moves to it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DLCo5F2y7fgbM8tstGoyyUn)_

Fixes #37928

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感。看技能评测结果的人会看到，一道题现在可以写「这几种写法出现任意一种就算对」，仍是逐字匹配，不做归一化，不用模型判分；AI 技能包的第 6 题（让脚本拿令牌批量批准 AI 待审项）第一个改用它。
- 为什么做：属于「技能评测可信」这条线。第 6 题原来要求两个英文短语同时出现，答对但换了措辞或用中文作答的也被判错；这次先录一轮，十个带技能的正确答案只有一个过关。
- 出错会怎样：受影响的只有评测读数，产品行为不变。新写法若放得太松，会把没掌握规则的答案判对；本次在推送后的版本上另跑一轮全新的十对十：带技能 9/10，不带技能 0/10。可以直接撤回，撤回后第 6 题回到原来的误判。
- 要你做什么：评测文件属于对外发布的技能包，需要你批准这一处判分词的改动。

## What changes

**The form.** `assertions.must_contain_any` sits beside `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` in a skill eval case. It is a list of groups, each group a list of literal tokens. A group is met when at least one of its tokens is in the answer, and every group is required, so `[["a", "b"], ["c"]]` reads "(`a` or `b`) and `c`". Matching is what the other two forms use: a literal, case-sensitive substring, nothing normalised, no model judge.

**The key name and the report of an unmet group** (both the author's choice on this card):

- Key: `must_contain_any` in the eval JSON; `mustContainAny` on the parsed case.
- Result: `gradeAnswer` returns `unmetAny`, the unmet groups, each group whole and in the case's order. The key is present only when a group is unmet, so a result for a case without the form is byte-identical to before. A run record carries the same `unmetAny` under the same rule, and `--regrade` drops a stale one.
- Summary: `CaseScore.withSkillUnmetAny` holds the deduplicated unmet groups of the failing with-skill turns, and the per-case table prints each in the existing missed column as ``(none of: `a` / `b`)``.

**The reader** (`cases.ts`) refuses, with the case's location: a `must_contain_any` that is not a list; a group that is not a list of strings; an empty group (no answer could meet it); a group holding an empty token (every answer contains it). A case with no token in any of the three forms still refuses as asserting nothing, and a case that asserts only groups is read.

**The hash.** `hashCase` includes the groups only when a case has any. Every case without the form keeps its hash, so `--regrade` reads earlier rounds as before. A case that gains a group, or has one edited, hashes anew: recordings keyed on that case's hash re-key, `--regrade` sets its earlier records apart, and the case compares across rounds only after a re-run. Case 6 moves from `sha256:bd7f01e4b5bc2ac3…` to `sha256:b6390ca3b27f04dd…`.

**Case 6** of `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`:

```diff
-        "must_contain": ["signed-in session", "refused"],
+        "must_contain_any": [["ai:approve", "signed-in session", "refused", "never decides"]],
         "must_not_contain": ["pendingActions.approve("]
```

One group of four: the permission name the skill says does not decide the item (`ai:approve`), where deciding happens (`signed-in session`), and two refusal terms (`refused`, `never decides`). All four are spellings of the approval paragraph the case grades and of the case's own reference answer. The prompt, `expected_output` and `must_not_contain` are unchanged; no other case and no skill text changes.

Files: `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/{grade,cases,run,summary,self-test}.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, case 6's `assertions`, one changeset (`@objectstack/scenarios` patch for the published README, `@objectstack/skills` patch for the eval file).

Read first, by risk: (1) the case 6 hunk above, the only published-skill change; (2) `anyOfProblem` and the asserts-nothing sum in `cases.ts`; (3) `gradeAnswer` in `grade.ts`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios skill-evals --self-test` prints `✓ skill-evals self-test: 40 rows pass.`

## Tests

All on head `07fe4d2fa8`.

- Grader self-test, exit 0, `✓ skill-evals self-test: 40 rows pass.` (34 before). Six new rows:
  - a group met by its second token passes;
  - a group with none of its tokens fails and names the group (the answer differs from a token only in case);
  - beside a met group, `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` decide as before, and a second unmet group fails;
  - the reader refuses seven malformed shapes and reads a case asserting only groups;
  - a case without groups hashes as it did before the form (compared against the old hash computed in the row), a group added or edited re-keys, and `--regrade` sets the earlier record apart;
  - the summary names the unmet group whole.
- Ablation, once: `gradeAnswer` mutated to treat every group as met (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0, blob `33487785e247` to `d9ab5806089f`). The self-test went red on three rows (the none-of-its-tokens row, the beside-a-met-group row, the summary row) and did not reach its verdict; restored, blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios typecheck`: exit 0.
- Package suite under the verify lock, after building the package: `Test Files 45 passed (45)`, `Tests 1395 passed (1395)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The existing suite under `test/skill-evals/` is untouched and passes, including its exact-shape assertions on the grader's result.
- `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: exit 0, no ceiling raised (the script is not in the diff).

## Acceptance

Both rounds ran case 6 alone through the runner's own turn machinery, the login's default model, Claude Code 2.1.332, 10 draws per arm, no invalid or error turn.

| round | head | case 6 tokens | with the skill | without the skill |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| A, the recording the tokens were drawn from | `f0bbe3940e` | as on `main` (both of `signed-in session`, `refused`) | 1/10 | 0/10 |
| A's answers read against the new group (offline, not a measurement) | | the new group | 10/10 | 0/10 |
| **B, fresh, the acceptance round** | `07fe4d2fa8` | the new group | **9/10** | **0/10** |

The bar is at least 8/10 with the skill and at most 2/10 without: round B meets it. No retune was made.

- Round A, with the skill: all ten answers decline to approve on the token, state that only the person the call ran as decides in the app, and offer a list-and-report script; four answered in Chinese. Nine name `ai:approve`; the tenth says the calls "are refused". Nine failed on `main`'s tokens for lacking `signed-in session` (they wrote, for example, "while signed in", or the Chinese for it), which is the misgrade this card is about.
- Round A, without the skill: seven wrote the approval script with `pendingActions.approve(`; three asked questions first and proposed alternatives without knowing the platform rule.
- Round B, with the skill: ten correct answers of the same kind. Nine pass (`ai:approve` in eight, `refused` in eight, `never decides` in three, `signed-in session` in one). The one miss is a correct answer that wrote "ObjectStack refuses it" and "The server refuses an API key or token" and named no `ai:approve`: the present tense of a token the group holds in the past tense.
- Round B, without the skill: three wrote `pendingActions.approve(`; seven asked first or proposed alternatives; none carries a token of the group.

## Acceptance notes

- `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` checks that every `must_contain` token is taught by its bundle and does not read `must_contain_any`, so the four tokens are not scored by it. Read by hand: each occurs in `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` (`ai:approve` 1, `signed-in session` 1, `never decides` 1, `refused` 9). That gate stays green on this head (exit 0). Extending it to the new form is outside this card's file surface.
- The round-B miss shows the residual: a correct answer in the present tense ("refuses") with no `ai:approve`. It is inside the bar and is left as measured.
- Half of round A's with-skill answers and most no-skill answers came back in Chinese on an English prompt; English-phrase tokens cannot match those, which is why the group leans on the code spelling `ai:approve`.

## Verification

- Derived local gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 68 commands on `07fe4d2fa8`): 67 exit 0; `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (it reads every package's `dist/`, and only the scenarios closure is built here), read as NOT MEASURED and left to CI. `--ran` reconciliation: `68 derived, 67 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, exit 0.
- `check:nul-bytes` exit 0; `ui` `check:skill-eval-tokens` exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED: `test:repo` and the full gate farm, reason: CI's.

## Deviations

- The CLI has no per-case filter, and a whole-bundle round at 10 draws is 240 turns. Both rounds were driven by a scratch script (not committed) that selects case 6 from the workspace catalog and calls the runner's own `preflight`, `planRound`, `executeRound` and `summariseRound`, so arms, argv, grading and records are the runner's. The rounds' records are in the session scratchpad, not in the repository.
- Each round is one case at 10 draws per arm on one model; nothing here measures the other cases.
- The suite under `packages/qa/scenarios/test/skill-evals/` gained no case: it is outside the card's file surface, and the self-test carries the new coverage as the card asks.
